title.narrative: Output 7.4. Increased capacity of Member States to provide adequate labour protection to workers in diverse forms of work arrangements, including on digital labour platforms, and in informal employment

description.narrative: In September 2023, the government, in consultation with the social partners, validated a country-level diagnosis on the penetration of digital labour platforms across different sectors of the economy. The diagnosis documented the experiences of women in accessing and performing work on such platforms, experiences of workers on accessing and performing work on digital labour platforms in multiple sectors of the Nigerian economy, with a focus on women workers; and the decent work deficits for women and men on digital labour platforms. The diagnosis was developed in consultation with social partners. The diagnosis was based on the sectors validated by the ILO’s tripartite constituents in September 2021. The sectors included beauty work (platforms and traditional), e-commerce, health care (platforms and traditional), medical consultation (platforms and traditional), online platform work (freelance and micro-task platforms), personal services and tutoring. With support from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF), ILO conducted a survey of 1092 workers across multiple sectors of the Nigerian economy and also conducted key informant interviews with representatives of governments, trade unions, employers’ organizations and platform companies to capture their perspectives, particularly regarding public policies frameworks to promote decent work in the platform economy. The country-level diagnosis also serves to enhance the capacities of the ILO’s tripartite constituents and to contribute towards the ongoing debate regarding public polices for advancing decent work for all on digital labour platforms.
